privacy.title: Privacy · Qalam
privacy.desc: What Qalam keeps, where it keeps it, and for how long.
privacy.lead: Qalam never asks for a name, a photo, a phone number or an address. Here is everything it keeps, where, for how long, and how to remove it.
privacy.phone_p1: Her lessons, stars, questions and settings stay on the phone she uses. A nickname she types never leaves the phone.
privacy.phone_p2: On a shared phone, each learner can have her own lock, so a brother or sister cannot open her work.
privacy.server_h: At the learning centre and online
privacy.server_p1: When she joins, the server keeps a picture and a number (such as “Book 27”), her year, and the consent her grown-up gave. It keeps a sealed fingerprint of her phone’s key, never the key.
privacy.server_p2: Questions are kept for 60 days, so a teacher can answer them. Which lessons were done is kept for 12 months, as counts without a name. A learner not seen for 12 months is deleted.
privacy.server_p3: At a village learning centre, all of this stays on the centre’s own computer. Online, Qalam keeps its records in the European Union.
privacy.bag_p1: The school bag is a locked copy of her progress, so her work can follow her to another phone, the learning centre or this website. It is locked on her phone with her 16-digit code before it leaves. Nobody can open it without that code, not even us.
privacy.bag_p2: A server keeps a bag only after her grown-up has agreed to the consent text that names it. The bag is deleted with her, and 12 months after it was last used. Without that agreement she can still carry her bag as a file.
privacy.bag_p3: The card with the code has no name, no address and not even the app’s name. Keep it like a house key. If someone else sees the code, make a new one in Settings.
privacy.site_p: This website sets no cookies, shows no adverts, tracks no one, and loads nothing from any other company. Your browser keeps only the language you chose. Visits are counted only from the server’s own totals.
privacy.consent_p: Before anything about a learner is kept, her grown-up, or she herself if she is an adult, agrees to one of these texts. They are drafts until reviewers and a solicitor sign them.
privacy.consent_online: Online and in the Android app
privacy.stop_p1: In Qalam’s Settings, “Stop sharing” deletes what the server keeps about her. Her lessons on the phone still work.
privacy.stop_p2: Removing a learner from a phone deletes her record on that phone.

families.title: For families · Qalam
families.desc: What Qalam costs in data, what it keeps, shared phones, and how to remove a learner.
families.lead: Free lessons for children from year 1 to year 12, and for adults, in Dari, Pashto and English. Qalam never asks for a name.
families.cost_p1: The first time, Qalam costs about {app_mb} MB of data, once. After that her lessons work with no internet.
families.cost_p2: Each lesson’s pictures and voice come the first time she opens it, a few KB each, and stay on the phone. On a learning centre’s Wi-Fi everything is free.
families.free_p1: Qalam is free. There are no adverts and nothing to buy.
families.free_p2: It never asks for a name, a photo, a phone number or an address. Each learner is a picture, such as a cup or a mountain, with a number.
families.shared_h: One phone for the whole family
families.shared_p1: Each child taps her own year and gets her own picture. “Who is learning” switches between them.
families.shared_p2: A grown-up can give each learner her own lock, so a brother or sister cannot open her work. Young children never get a lock to forget.
families.app_p: On Android, the app can ring the school bells even when Qalam is closed. You can get it from this website, at the learning centre, or from a friend’s phone by Bluetooth.
families.bag_p: Her school bag card has a 16-digit code. With it, her lessons, stars and plan come to a new phone. Keep the card like a house key.
families.bag_lost: Without the card or its code, nobody can open her school bag, not even us.
families.today_p: On a borrowed phone, choose “Just for today”: her work goes to her school bag when she taps Done, and nothing stays on that phone.
families.iphone_p: On an iPhone, Safari can clear Qalam after a week without use. Add Qalam to the Home Screen, and print her card.
families.remove_p: In Qalam’s Settings, “Stop sharing” deletes what the server keeps about her, and removing a learner deletes her from the phone.
teachers.title: For teachers · Qalam
teachers.desc: Class codes, printed worksheets, the learning centre, and the teacher’s page.
teachers.lead: Your class learns on its own phones. You see who is learning, answer their questions, and print worksheets for the whole class.
teachers.codes_p1: Each class has a code of eight letters and numbers, such as {class_code}. The learning centre’s admin makes it and prints it on class cards with a QR code.
teachers.codes_p2: A learner scans the card, or taps “I have a class code” and types it. From then on her questions reach you, under her picture and number.
teachers.print_p1: Every lesson ends with one worksheet. At a learning centre with a printer, you can print it for the whole class.
teachers.print_p2: A learner checks her own sheet with “Check my sheet”: she types her answers and gets hints, never the answer.
teachers.hub_p1: A learning centre is one small computer with its own Wi-Fi and a printer, and no internet. Phones join its Wi-Fi and open {hub_addr}.
teachers.hub_p2: Lessons, worksheets, answers to questions and the teacher’s page all work there, free.
teachers.lock_p: If a learner forgets her lock, the teacher’s page gives a one-time code for her picture and number. Nothing else about her is shown.
teachers.page_p: At a learning centre, open it with the centre’s teacher PIN. Online, you sign in with the address your school gave you.
partners.title: About Qalam
partners.desc: What Qalam is, how it is made, and how you can help.
partners.lead: Qalam is a free school on a phone for Afghan children and adults.
partners.what_p1: Lessons from year 1 to year 12, and reading and numbers for adults, in Dari, Pashto and English, with a voice on every sentence and a worksheet on paper.
partners.what_p2: It works on cheap phones and without the internet, and at village learning centres: one small computer with Wi-Fi and a printer.
partners.how_p1: Every lesson is checked by a native speaker and a teacher before it is final; until then it is marked as a draft. Religious lessons are written with a Hanafi scholar.
partners.how_p2: Qalam keeps no names, shows no adverts and loads nothing from other companies.
partners.help_p: Check lessons in Dari or Pashto, teach at a learning centre, or support a centre’s computer and printer.
partners.contact_soon: An email address for partners will be here once Qalam’s own web address is set up.
